title: Bigger, more careful, the best
goal: Compare two or more things without “more better”
intro: To compare two things, add -er to short adjectives (cheap → cheaper) or put “more” before long ones (more expensive), then use “than”. For three or more, use “the” + -est or “the most”. Never use both: “more better” is wrong.

examples: This phone is more expensive than mine.
She is the most talented singer here.

rules.rule: Irregular: good → better → the best; bad → worse → the worst; far → further.
examples: Your English is better than mine.
That was the worst day of my life.

mistakes.wrong: She is more elder than me.

mistakes.why: Senior, junior, superior and prior take “to”.

mistakes.right: Mumbai is the most crowded city.

mistakes.wrong: She is more smarter than him.

ex.q: This is ___ film I have ever seen.
My brother is two years ___ me.
She is junior ___ me in the office.
Your idea is more better than mine.
ex.fixed: Your idea is better than mine.

ex.q: He is the most tallest boy in the class.
ex.fixed: He is the tallest boy in the class.

ex.q: This is the ___ day of the year. (hot)
Correct this: “My new job is more better than my old job.”
a: My new job is better than my old job
My new job is better than my old one

talk: Compare two cities you know: which is bigger, cleaner, more expensive, and which is the best place to live? Use at least five comparisons.
